headline: PM says public trust is healthcare’s biggest challenge
summary: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina promises reforms after doctors and students raise key concerns regarding the healthcare system.
details: The Prime Minister has identified the lack of public trust as the most significant challenge facing the healthcare sector.
Following discussions with doctors and students, she has promised to implement reforms to address critical healthcare issues.
The move comes as medical professionals and students highlight systemic gaps and areas for improvement in the country's medical services.
The government aims to restore confidence in the healthcare system through these promised structural and operational changes.

headline: Flood and landslides kill 44 in Bangladesh; over 1 million affected
summary: Heavy rains and overflowing rivers have submerged vast areas in seven districts, displacing over a million people and causing widespread devastation.
details: At least 44 people have died in Bangladesh due to flash floods and landslides triggered by incessant rainfall and overflowing rivers, the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief reported. The disaster has affected over 1 million people across seven southeastern and northeastern districts.

The affected districts include Khagrachhari, Rangamati, Bandarban, Cox's Bazar, Chittagong, Moulvibazar, and Habiganj. A total of 386 unions and 11 municipalities in 58 upazilas have been inundated, leaving 267,918 families waterlogged.

Cox's Bazar reported the highest number of casualties, with 23 deaths attributed to landslides and floods. Among the deceased in Cox's Bazar, 10 were local residents and 13 were Rohingya refugees. 24 people were injured in the district.

In the port city of Chittagong, 11 people were killed and 12 injured in flood-related incidents, including building collapses. The hilly districts of Bandarban and Rangamati also reported fatalities, with 6 and 3 deaths respectively.

Moulvibazar in the northeast recorded one death due to flooding. The full extent of the damage is still being assessed, but the widespread inundation has disrupted daily life and livelihoods for millions.

Authorities are working to provide aid and relief to the affected populations. The Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief is coordinating rescue and rehabilitation efforts across the impacted regions.
